entries.reason: Recomputed from the stems. MC04-FDP-02: 1/4 of 40 = 10, half = 20. MC04-FDP-07: 3/8 of 32 = 12, 20 left, a quarter = 5, half = 10. MC04-FDP-08: 3/5 of 40 = 24, 16 left, a quarter used (4) leaves 12, half used (8) leaves 8. All three values are present as options; the description's 20 for 1/4 of 40 (key 10) is right. Not a duplicate: maths-78 names 25% read as a half, a percentage-to-fraction conversion, and its hint (50%, 25%) speaks of percentages none of these stems contain, so it is untrue to the move on all three rows. maths-24, -75 and -82 hold the other values (160, 40, 8/6) and are different mistakes. The hint defines a quarter (true wherever a quarter is asked, not a claim about one item) and then describes the move; sentences of 12 and 9 words, plain British English. The id restricts it to a quarter halved, so it refuses halving where a third or other fraction is asked. Also fits MC03-FDP-07 (1/4 of 60) if ever tagged there.

Recomputed. MC05-GEOM-06: triangle angle on the line = 180 - 140 = 40, third = 180 - 40 - 30 = 110; the mistake 180 - 140 - 30 = 10, present as an option. MC02-GEOM-06: 180 - 110 = 70, third = 180 - 70 - 25 = 85; the mistake 180 - 110 - 25 = 45, present. Every number in the description (10, 110, 140, 30, 40) is right. A real and common error: the angle on the straight line taken as an angle of the triangle. No ACTIVE entry names it: the current tags are wrong for these values (maths-100's halving of 180 gives neither 10 nor 45; maths-71 requires an unused number, and all three given numbers are used); maths-89 (290/265) and maths-proc-01 (40) are different mistakes. The hint describes a move (check the angle is inside before using it) and a general fact true on every row, since the entry only lands where a straight line is given; sentences of 12 and 8 words. Narrow: it names an angle beside a triangle on a straight line, so it refuses wrong angle totals and stopping early.

Recomputed every carrier. Counting on from the price to the next pound (the bridge) and then to the money given, keeping only the second jump: MC01 £5 - £3.50 bridge 50p, gives £1.00 (key £1.50); MC02 £8 - £2.60 bridge 40p, £5.00 (key £5.40); MC03 £8 - £5.60 bridge 40p, £2.00 (key £2.40); MC04 £7 - £2.80 bridge 20p, £4.00 (key £4.20); MC05 £8 - £3.40 bridge 60p, £4.00 (key £4.60). The description's MC03 figures are right, and each value is £1 below maths-83's on every row. FAIR DISTRACTOR: yes. The stem asks for the change, an exact calculation with no 'about' or 'estimate'; every option is written to the penny, so £5.00 against £5.40 is 40p of change not given, clearly wrong and not an acceptable approximation. Being close to the key is what makes it diagnostic, not unfair. DISTINCT FROM maths-99: yes as a mistake, but the overlap is wider than the drafter's 'why' states. This mistake equals the money given minus the price rounded UP to the next pound; maths-99 (rounding to the nearest and not compensating) rounds UP whenever the pence are 50p or more, so it gives the SAME value on MC01, MC02, MC03 and MC04 (£1.00, £5.00, £2.00, £4.00), not on MC01 alone. Only MC05 separates them: £3.40 rounds down, so maths-99 gives £5.00 (already maths-83's value) and this entry gives £4.00. The procedures differ (exact counting on with a dropped jump against estimating and not adjusting), MC05 shows the values can part, and neither existing entry's hint teaches the counting-on move, so the entry is warranted. But on MC01-MC04 the value alone cannot tell the two apart, and which tag any option there carries is a separate reviewer ruling that this attestation does not make. The hint describes the counting-on method and is true on every change row, including the multi-item and £10-note rows (e.g. MC04-MEAS-04, £6.05 to £7 then to £10); sentences of 12 and 7 words. Narrow: it applies only where a bridge to the next pound exists.
